findings.title: Second downsize definition overwrites the existing four-argument method
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading. Defining self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 replaces the self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) defined at line 145. Existing callers that pass separate width and height will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), breaking thumbnail/image downsizing outside this new upload path. The two signatures must be merged into one method that accepts either a dimension string or width/height.

findings.title: Downsizing uses an extensionless tempfile path, so ImageMagick cannot infer formats and animation is lost
findings.body: The uploaded/downloaded tempfile paths (file.tempfile and FileHelper.download's tempfile) normally have no image extension. OptimizedImage.downsize passes tempfile.path as both input and output to `convert`, so ImageMagick cannot infer the output format from the destination extension and conversion can fail. In addition, OptimizedImage.optimize only selects the animated instructions when the source path ends in .GIF, which an extensionless tempfile never does, so downsize_instructions uses `#{from}[0]` and reduces an animated GIF to its first frame despite passing allow_animation. The image should be downsized via a temp file carrying the original extension (and a separate output path) before replacing the upload.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure and never verifies the result is within the limit
findings.body: The loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's boolean return value and, after at most five 80% reductions, unconditionally proceeds to Upload.create_for. If conversion fails (unsupported/corrupt/SVG image) it pointlessly retries five times on the same in-place file, which may have been truncated by the failed convert, and if five reductions still leave the file larger than max_image_size_kb.kilobytes the oversized upload is passed on anyway to be rejected (or stored over the limit). The code should abort/retry sensibly on failure and check the final size before creating the upload.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores per-type site settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each honored the admin-configured limit. Replacing it with a fixed 10MB means sites with a lower max_attachment_size_kb/max_image_size_kb let users select files the server will reject, and sites configured above 10MB incorrectly block allowed files with a 'file too large' alert citing 10240 KB. The same hardcoded value at line 246 makes the 413 error message state the wrong configured maximum. The client limit needs to remain setting/type-aware (at minimum, the raised cap should apply only where the server actually downsizes, i.e. images).

findings.title: Remote-download cap hardcoded to 10MB bypasses the configured image limit for non-image/API cases
findings.body: FileHelper.download now always allows 10 megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. The compensating downsize loop only runs when FileHelper.is_image?(filename) is true, so any API URL fetch whose filename is not recognized as an image (or whose image later fails to downsize below the limit) can now pull and store a file up to 10MB regardless of the admin's configured maximum. The raised download cap should be conditional on the file actually being a downsizable image, with the configured limit retained otherwise.
